questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Courses in English and nice weather

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. UQ was super helpful with everything introductory. Though, a little confusion about which introduction "classes" to attend from time to time. It seemed crucial to attend everything, but I guess it wouldn't matter much if you were to miss something.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Different introduction seminars - both academic, social etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Do not wait until you have arrived to search for housing. I, and a lot of my friends and co-students struggled to find housing (due to a bigger demand relative to the supply).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's great. I really enjoyed living off campus, as I got the opportunity to experience much more of Brisbane. I found a room in West End, and I loved it there - great location (close to St. Lucia and CBD) and cool vibe.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I'm not really sure what is meant by registration process, but getting my student card and everything was pretty smooth.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A student central with very knowledgable students were available. And a lot of other platforms and services available for various matters.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 4/4. I got all the classes I wished for. I changed one course for another once I got to Brisbane, as I figured it would be too much work.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's easy. And UQ is happy to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you're going on your masters/postgrad., expect a heavier workload than your undergrad. co-students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
It's a very different way of studying than what I've been used to at KU. Many assignments during the semester and a greater expectation to actively participate in the courses.
I spent a lot more time on the classes than what I had anticipated before going, and it payed off (grade-wise), but don't expect it to be super easy just because the grades will be transferred to pass/failed. I guess it depends on the specific courses though.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Larger focus on active participation. More class discussions etc. The teaching style was more of a seminar than lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intercultural Communication
Ethics and Human Rights
International Relations in Asia-Pacific
Gender, Peace and Security in Local and Global Perspective

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would very much recommend the Ethics and Human Rights course. Emma was a great lecturer, super nice.
The Gender, Peace and Security courses was also very interesting, and Nicole the lecturer was both inspiring and very knowledgeable.
The Intercultural Communication was an easy course, but I didn't like the lecturer and the course was very focused on the gaps and differences between Australian culture and Chinese culture, as the lecturer was Chinese and 95% of the students taking the course were Chinese.
International Relations was a very cool course as well, but I struggled a bit, since I didn't have any prior knowledge about the region. But very interesting course and I learned a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I expected it to be expensive, so nothing really unexpected, but super cheap coffee at cafés and very expensive beers at the bottle shops. Otherwise very much as in DK in terms of supermarket costs and eating/going out etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above. Cheap coffee, expensive beers from bottle shop, cheaper drinks and beers at bars/clubs. A bit cheaper eating out. Cheap local transport.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many social clubs. wanted to give everything a try, but obviously had to prioritise. Many sports clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Anything you can think of!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go see the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast - great for weekend trips. I went to Sydney for a weekend also and went on a road trip to Cairns when the semester had ended.
I also wish I had more time and money to simply explore Brisbane and the food scene there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Australians are super friendly and welcoming. Loved how they were genuinely interested in getting to know you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't socialize much with my fellow local students, as I didn't have any courses with local students. Most of my courses were with other international students. I spent a lot of time with other Danes - which was also great.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you're a masters student, don't stress about everything you feel like you need to see and do when in Australia. Try also to enjoy your time at UQ. It's a great experience to study at another university, and if you, as I, spend a lot of time on your courses, it helps if you try to appreciate the opportunity in this.
Enjoy Brisbane and try to make it your home. I got to see many places on the east coast, but I also wanted to spend time in Brisbane so that I actually felt it as my home. Don't try to escape Brisbane.
Put in the needed work, but don't stress about the grades etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Many rewarding things, can't single out one. The people I met, the things I learned (from UQ and from locals), etc.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding accommodation and occasionally the time difference and time managing uni and fun stuff.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
